name: Form Action Button
tagline: A model-driven form button that raises an event a form script can handle, confirm and answer.

limitations: There is no form script behind this demo. On a real form the press reaches a handler registered with addEventHandler("onAction", fn), and that handler is the whole point of the control — here it reaches nothing, so what you are pressing is the button rather than the action.

The confirmation dialog is the demo's stand-in for the platform's. The control finds openConfirmDialog, asks it, and raises onAction only on a confirm, which is its path on a form too; what differs is the dialog itself, drawn by the demo rather than by the app, so it does not carry your app's theme. The inline two-step the control falls back to on a host with no dialog is not shown here — the screenshots have it.
The busy and result states cannot be reached from a preset. A handler drives them by calling setBusy() and setResult() back into the control, and there is no handler here to call them.

Privilege gating does nothing here. It needs the table the form is on, which a form publishes through mode.contextInfo and this demo does not, so the control declines to gate — the correct behaviour on such a host, and it looks like nothing happening. The demo would grant every privilege in any case, so a denied button could not be shown either.

presets.name: A plain button
presets.description: One press, one event. The default configuration, and the one most buttons want.

presets.name: Confirmed, with a glyph
presets.description: On a form this opens the platform's confirmation dialog; here the demo draws a stand-in with the same title, question and button. Confirm and the event is raised — watch the outputs. Cancel, or press Escape, and nothing happens.

presets.name: Writing the signal column
presets.description: Every press writes into the bound column, which is what lets a business rule or a workflow see it. Watch the outputs: the value changes on every press, because a column set to the same value twice fires no OnChange at all.

presets.name: A long label, confirmed
presets.description: The button wraps rather than overflowing — the layout a narrow form column actually produces. Its confirmation takes the default title and question, with Confirm submission on the button.
